title: Friction GPS + Feature Companion Brief
high_level_summary: Synthesize recent frontline reports into an action-oriented map that pinpoints operational friction and 6 small, testable feature proposals (microrequests) that reduce failure modes for high-value customers.
prioritized_requests: Priority A — 'Latency-safe tier': customers with synchronous user-facing endpoints want a guaranteed fast-fail/low-latency path (SLO: p95 <= 120ms for light prompts). Rationale: repeated reports of UI timeouts and fallback to retries. Impact: reduces visible timeouts and support tickets. Suggested pilot: dedicated small T4 pool + routing policy. Rough KPI: reduce timeout tickets by 40% in pilot accounts.

Priority B — 'Prompt prefix cache API': an easy key-based prefix caching endpoint for canonical system messages and persona prompts. Rationale: multiple customers serving repetitive system prompts (bots, assistants) note redundant token costs and cold KV-cache penalties. Impact: token cost down, latency down for long contexts. Pilot: expose new header 'X-Cache-Key' + eviction policy. KPI: 20–30% token spend reduction on tested flows.

Priority C — 'Inference diagnostic trace v0': lightweight per-request trace id surfaced in responses, plus a debug view that shows which model variant and fallback path served the request. Rationale: troubleshooting is slow because teams can't correlate user errors with server-side decisions. Impact: fewer support escalations and faster RCA. Pilot: enable for enterprise accounts only.

Priority D — 'Embeddings dedup prefilter': a client-side library snippet + server flag to do cheap hashing to avoid embedding near-duplicates. Rationale: customers doing semantic search ingest see wasted embedding spend when duplicates auto-ingested. Impact: cost savings, index quality improvement. Pilot: prefilter mode in SDK + server opt-in.

Priority E — 'Rollout throttling hooks': per-customer rollout window controls to limit percent/throughput during model rollouts for stability-sensitive customers. Rationale: some customers reported regressions during org-wide rollouts. Impact: smoother canaries & fewer rollback events. Pilot: add 'max-pps' and 'traffic-slope' knobs in rollout UI/API.

Priority F — 'Usage anomaly alert pack': a standard alert template (email + Slack) for sudden token cost spikes tied to model changes or mis-routed traffic. Rationale: customers miss big cost regressions overnight. Impact: quicker mitigation, reduced bill surprises. Pilot: default thresh 3x baseline; customers can tune.
evidence_snippets: "We had three sessions today where the assistant just timed out; users thought the whole app was down. We had to roll back to old model overnight." — Fintech internal ops
"Most of our messages begin with the same 400-token system instructions — doubling our token bill. If we could cache that server-side we'd save a lot." — Marketplace CTO
"When model A is overloaded it silently falls back to model B and we see quality regressions; it's impossible to trace which model returned the answer." — Platform eng lead
"Our customer success engineers are constantly triaging huge embedding spend on duplicated records. We need cheap de-dup." — Search product manager
usage_patterns: High-frequency short prompts from chat widgets — latency-sensitive, single-turn interactions.
Large-batch background embedding pipelines — cost-sensitive and tolerant of retries.
Hybrid flows mixing hosted + dedicated endpoints — customers expect identical behavior across modes.
Onboarding misconfigurations (wrong model variant, unlimited concurrency) lead to sudden cost spikes.
Heavy use of identical system messages across sessions (candidate for prefix caching).
recommended_experiments: Experiment 1: Launch a 6-week pilot for 5 customers with 'Latency-safe tier' behind a feature flag; compare p95 latency, user-reported timeouts, and support ticket volume vs control.
Experiment 2: Deliver 'Prompt prefix cache API' as beta to two customers with predictable system prompts; instrument token delta and latency delta per request.
Experiment 3: Enable 'Inference diagnostic trace v0' for a single SRE + CS partner; measure mean time to resolution (MTTR) on related incidents.
Experiment 4: Publish an SDK prefilter snippet and A/B the dedup filter on a dataset ingestion job to estimate embedding cost savings and false-positive rate.
risk_flags: Security: prefix cache must not introduce cross-tenant leakage — require encryption/tenant-scoped keys.
Operational: adding dedicated latency tiers increases capacity planning complexity and potential for under-utilization.
Product: rollout throttling might frustrate customers expecting full-traffic rollouts; needs clear UX and opt-in semantics.
Measurement: cost savings claims rely on decent instrumentation — we need standardized metrics before public claims.
rough_effort_estimates: Latency-safe tier — Medium (4–6 wks eng + 2 wk infra runway): requires routing policy + small dedicated pool config.
Prompt prefix cache API — Low/Medium (3–5 wks): API surface + eviction and tenant-scope security.
Inference diagnostic trace v0 — Low (2–3 wks): surface trace ids + UI lookup; deeper tracing is follow-on.
Embeddings dedup prefilter — Low (2–3 wks): SDK snippet + optional server-side flag for datasets.
Rollout throttling hooks — Medium (3–6 wks): UI + policy enforcement, plus guardrails for legacy rollouts.
Usage anomaly alert pack — Very Low (1–2 wks): templated alerts wired to existing metrics stream.

notes_to_self: This doc is intentionally prescriptive — goal is to convert fuzzy asks into bounded experiments. Expect pushback on effort estimates; get quick buy-in by proposing small opt-in pilots.
